q: What is the recommended percentage increment when vertically scaling a winning ad set's daily budget?
explain: Increments of 15-20% maintain algorithm stability without triggering a learning phase reset.

q: What is Marketing Efficiency Ratio (MER)?
options: Total Net Company Revenue ÷ Total Paid Ad Spend across all channels
Cost Per Click divided by CPM
explain: MER measures holistic blended marketing efficiency across the entire business.

q: In an Advantage+ Shopping Campaign (ASC), what setting prevents overspending on past customers?
explain: An existing customer budget cap (e.g. 10-15%) forces ASC to allocate most budget to net-new cold buyers.

q: What is a Geo-Lift experiment used for?
options: Measuring true incremental sales lift by comparing ad-exposed regions against holdout regions
Increasing ad delivery in hilly areas
explain: Geo-lift holdout tests prove whether ads generated incremental revenue that wouldn't happen organically.

q: When scaling ad spend from ₹5,000/day to ₹50,000/day, what is the most common operational bottleneck?
options: Creative velocity (producing enough fresh hooks to outpace fatigue)
explain: At scale, audiences burn through creatives rapidly; without continuous fresh creative testing, CAC explodes.

q: What does a consolidated account structure prioritize over heavy fragmentation?
options: Feeding maximum conversion signals into fewer machine learning algorithms to exit learning fast
explain: Consolidated structures give Meta's AI sufficient data density (~50 weekly events) to optimize effectively.

q: What is Media Mix Modeling (MMM)?
options: A Photoshop plugin for video editing
A top-down statistical regression technique that estimates cross-channel sales impact over time
Mixing Hindi and English voiceovers in ads
Running ads on Facebook and Instagram simultaneously
explain: MMM is a privacy-first statistical regression tool used by mature brands to analyze macro channel influence.

q: What is the primary difference between intent-capture (Google) and demand-generation (Meta)?
options: Google captures people actively searching for solutions; Meta introduces products to people who didn't know they needed them
Google only runs text; Meta only runs videos
Google is free; Meta is paid
explain: Google captures existing search demand; Meta creates net-new desire and consumer interest.

q: What is a 'holdout group' in marketing incrementality testing?
options: A group of users or geographic regions intentionally kept unexposed to ads to measure baseline sales
Customers who refused to pay on delivery
A team of media buyers on standby
Ad accounts paused for policy review
explain: A holdout group measures what sales would occur naturally without advertising, isolating true lift.

q: If an ad account is restricted due to suspicious billing, what is the first operational step?
options: Submit a verified business PAN/GST statement and official ID in Account Quality
explain: Formal appeals with official company registration and billing proofs resolve financial flags safely.

q: What is Creative Fatigue?
options: When a copywriter gets tired of writing
When an ad's audience has seen it so many times that CTR decays and acquisition costs increase
When an ad is paused overnight
explain: Repeated exposure leads to banner blindness, declining CTR, and higher auction penalties.

q: What does the ICE prioritization framework stand for in testing roadmaps?
explain: ICE evaluates potential tests by estimated Impact, Confidence in result, and Ease of execution.

q: What is the danger of setting a campaign budget too low across 30 ad sets?
options: Ad sets get stuck in 'Learning Limited' and CPMs increase due to data starvation
explain: Data starvation keeps ad sets in Learning Limited, causing volatility and high costs.

q: What is View-Through Attribution?
options: Counting a conversion when someone views an ad without clicking, but converts within 24 hours
Tracking users who watch ads on television
Viewing competitor ads in Ad Library
explain: View-through credits ads when a user converts shortly after viewing, even without an initial click.

q: How should ad performance be reported to a non-technical CEO?
options: In terms of top-line revenue, blended CAC, ad spend, and net contribution margin
Presenting raw 40-column spreadsheets of vanity metrics
Focusing exclusively on frequency and EMQ
explain: Executives prioritize commercial outcomes: Revenue, customer acquisition costs, and profit margins.

q: What is horizontal scaling in media buying?
options: Testing new creative angles, new audiences, and expanded geographic regions
Increasing daily budget on one ad set by 500%
explain: Horizontal scaling expands reach through new creative concepts and target segments.

q: Why is Last-Click attribution often biased against Top-of-Funnel video ads?
options: It gives 100% credit to the final search or direct visit, ignoring the video that created the original desire
explain: Last-click ignores the discovery assists provided by awareness and educational video ads.

q: What is the primary role of an Agency Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)?
options: Ensuring naming conventions, pre-flight launch checklists, and kill/scale rules are executed consistently
explain: SOPs enforce quality, eliminate human errors, and institutionalize proven testing rules.

q: What is a dark post in social advertising?
options: An unpublished page post promoted purely as an ad, not appearing on the main public brand profile grid
explain: Dark posts run in feeds as targeted ads without cluttering the brand's public profile feed.

q: In a mature e-commerce media plan, what is a typical healthy allocation between Meta and Google?
explain: Meta generates new demand while Google captures high-intent search and shopping volume.
